title: Eliminate high canonical charges while retaining the common bath and relative detuning vertex
statement: For the linear-profile full-charge model with |eta|<=1/8, the stated energy region and q=2|lambda|sqrt(2C/E_R+2Vg/E_R^2)<=1/2, normal truncation afterN has first-block resolvent error<=q^(2N)/(E_R(1-q)). The transverse Schur selfenergy obeys |Sigma_x|<=(16lambda^2|eta|/E_R)Y^2 with no eta-independent remainder.

requires: Actual linear-profile full canonical Hamiltonian, form domains/regulators and explicit real/complex-z energy region; fixed E_R satisfying the walk-majorant gate.
provides: For the linear-profile full-charge model with |eta|<=1/8, the stated energy region and q=2|lambda|sqrt(2C/E_R+2Vg/E_R^2)<=1/2, normal truncation afterN has first-block resolvent error<=q^(2N)/(E_R(1-q)). The transverse Schur selfenergy obeys |Sigma_x|<=(16lambda^2|eta|/E_R)Y^2 with no eta-independent remainder.
assumptions: No unchanged finite-aperture application; no finite-T global energy cutoff after the thermodynamic limit, Gaussian common bath or free Coulomb-gas vertex. A relative Schur coefficient is not a transition rate.
costs: Normal levelsN, all Gaussian matrix/integration/bit work, common selfenergy and reconstruction metric remain paid. Error is relative to the displayed form scale, not an unknown vanishing infrared signal.
contract.units: E_R,z and Sigma are energies, q dimensionless; resolvent error has inverse-energy units. Y^2 form and C,Vg use the actual coordinate convention.
contract.obstruction: A small discarded-level population or absolute error cannot justify replacing a fixed microscopic correction by a free spin thermal model.

body: Keep the entire Gaussian Hilbert space when projecting only normal j=0. The exact Schur inverse retains Sigma0, the common energy-dependent correction, and E_R eta-Sigma_x as transverse operator. A uniform Gaussian energy form controls Y, and a positive Jacobi walk majorant bounds all missing paths. Resolve the unbounded d in the difference identity to obtain the relative eta bound and its sign. Full-eigenvector reconstruction has metric I+partial_E Sigma; common spring softening persists at fixed E_R. Compressed resolvent equality is not an equality of thermal ensembles or a physical TLS splitting.

evidence.range_scope: Exact full-charge Schur reduction, normal-tail/relative eta control, common correction, reconstruction metric and low-energy versus finite-T boundary.
evidence.status: Exact frozen source bytes; scientific acceptance is scoped to actual version-bound review.

review.scope: Completed source-exposed author review of finite-aperture square/log-partition and bounded-Q tail/dipole bounds, nonlinear curvature plus full uncentered KMS contact and all-mode absolute excess majorants, exact full-ladder sector response/finite-pulse domain bounds, and Schur/Jacobi normal-tail/relative detuning forms including the common correction and reconstruction metric. Final acquired root and reciprocal whole reconstructions pin all four exact versions. The finite-aperture static theorem is not silently composed with the differently specified linear-profile pulse/resolvent. Numerical scripts were read statically, not replayed or accepted as an infinite-bath proof.
